blocks.text: The reality of crisis management for executive assistants

A crisis in the office often looks like a series of urgent emails and calendar invites. You are the one who has to filter the noise. You must decide what needs immediate attention and what can wait. This is where executive assistant problem solving examples become practical tools for daily survival.
Why crisis management becomes a bottleneck

The main issue is context switching. You move from an email in Outlook to a calendar in Google Calendar to a document in Word. Each switch takes time. Each switch adds risk for errors. If you hold too much information in your head, you will eventually hit a wall.

items: Too many tabs open in Safari or Chrome.
Manual tracking of action items in emails.
Lack of a centralized view for urgent tasks.

blocks.text: You do not need expensive software to improve your workflow. Start by standardizing how you handle incoming requests. Create a template for meeting requests. This ensures you always have the right information before you even look at a calendar.
Use the macOS Spotlight search (⌘ + Space) to find files instantly. Stop clicking through folders in Finder.
blocks.title: Use system tools

blocks.text: Lazur helps you stay in the flow. When you are overwhelmed by a long email thread, hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur to summarize the key requests. This clears your screen and your mind.

faq.question: How can I improve my decision support skills?
faq.answer: Focus on gathering all facts before presenting options to your executive. Use clear, concise summaries.

faq.question: What is the best way to handle urgent emails?
faq.answer: Use a triage system. Label emails by urgency and handle the most critical ones first.

fixes.title: Front load decisions
fixes.text: Handle the most complex tasks first thing in the morning when your energy is highest.

fixes.title: Standardize triage
fixes.text: Use consistent labels for emails to quickly identify tasks that require immediate action.
